lede: Donald Trump has made Stephen Miller his chief of staff after the midterm rout, OpenAI is reportedly adding another US$11 billion at a US$1.25 trillion valuation, and Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro is in customers' hands. Fresh Singapore AI startup news was thin today, so that section has two stories instead of five.
stocks_note: Latest closes: New York, Friday 6 November (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Friday 6 November (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. Apple reported fourth-quarter results on 2 November; no other earnings dates seen.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple's newsroom has been quiet since 3 November, when it said the redesigned Health app is gaining more languages. This week Apple told press that more than 100,000 apps are now optimised for iPhone Duo, set 20 November for the reopening of its redesigned Carlsbad store, and put its extended holiday return policy into effect from today.

items.headline: Apple's DOJ antitrust fight pulls Epic, Samsung, Oura and Roblox into subpoena disputes
items.summary: Several tech companies are resisting subpoenas tied to the ongoing antitrust case between Apple and the Justice Department. The pushback shows how widely the litigation reaches across the industry, with rivals and partners now arguing over what they must hand over.

items.headline: Apple could face congressional scrutiny over ICE tracking apps and political donations
items.summary: Reuters and the Washington Post report that Apple is among the tech giants that may be investigated once Democrats take control of Congress. Topics include how it handled apps that track immigration enforcement and its donations to President Trump.

items.headline: Hands-on with Apple's new OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro
items.summary: The new PROLED MacBook Pro reached customers today, and MacRumors picked one up to try it. The site's first look focuses on the touchscreen and the new display, the headline changes to Apple's pro laptop line.

items.headline: Two more Apple products land next week to close out the launch run
items.summary: Apple's long run of releases ends next week, with the HomeView smart home hub and the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K due to arrive. MacRumors says that completes the wave of products announced over the past few weeks.

items.headline: Seventh fugitive arrested over Cambodia-based scam syndicate that targeted Singaporeans
items.summary: Police have arrested another person linked to the syndicate, the seventh so far. It is believed to be tied to at least 528 scam cases in Singapore, with losses of about S$53 million.

items.headline: UMNO pays Najib Razak's S$15.8 million fine after crowdfunding drive
items.summary: The party covered the fine imposed on the former Malaysian prime minister after raising money from supporters. Najib will now serve out his sentence under house arrest.

items.headline: M1 hit by data breach on 30 October, customer data exposed
items.summary: The telco says an incident on 30 October exposed some customer data. It says no payment card details and no financial or banking information were compromised.

items.headline: Telemedicine provider Doctor Anywhere reports a data breach
items.summary: The company described a malicious cyber incident in which an unknown third party gained unauthorised access. It is the second Singapore consumer-facing breach disclosed in two days.

items.headline: Fresh graduates say they will keep trying as the job market tightens
items.summary: Landing a full-time job straight after graduation is getting harder, according to students interviewed. Many say they are widening how they search rather than giving up.

items.headline: Voters removed in seven states and UTs can re-enrol without Form 6
items.summary: The Election Commission says people deleted from rolls during the special intensive revision can return to them without filling the usual form. Delhi and six other states and union territories are covered.

items.headline: Falling gold prices lift jewellery sales on Dhanteras
items.summary: A drop in the gold price brought buyers into shops for Dhanteras, the traditional day for buying gold, and pushed up jewellery sales compared with what retailers had feared.

items.headline: Maharashtra crackdown ahead of Diwali hits Zepto, Blinkit, Biryani By Kilo and D-Mart
items.summary: State food-safety enforcement covered quick-commerce platforms and well-known food chains. In Mumbai, licences were suspended for Zepto's Worli outlet and for Blinkit's operator, Blink Commerce.

items.headline: High Court judge vacancies at a ten-year low of 26 per cent, yet pendency keeps growing
items.summary: Fewer High Court posts are empty than at any point in a decade, but the backlog of pending cases has not shrunk. The gap suggests appointments alone are not clearing the queue.

items.headline: Supreme Court ruling on BBMB arrears is a win for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
items.summary: The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh's 7.19 per cent share of the power produced by the Bhakra Beas projects. The chief minister called it a victory for the state.

items.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
items.summary: The promotion comes after Republican losses in the midterms. Miller has been a close aide since 2016 and shaped the administration's hardline immigration policy.

items.headline: New wave of bomb threats hits European airlines
items.summary: Scores of flights across Europe have received threats this week and no explosives have been found. A Russian extremist group has denied sending them, and no link to threats against media outlets has been established.

items.headline: Pope Leo starts a 12-day Latin America tour weeks after lung surgery
items.summary: The pontiff arrived in Uruguay and will also visit Argentina and Peru. He told reporters he is in fairly good shape after having part of a lung removed last month.

items.headline: Houthis say 30 killed as Saudi strikes hit a market in Taiz
items.summary: The Houthis say several strikes hit a market in an area they control in Taiz province, where fighting has been heavy. The claim has not been independently confirmed in the report.

items.headline: US presses China to honour its Busan trade deal commitments
items.summary: Washington wants Beijing to deliver on the Trump-Xi deal meant to ease tariffs and tech restrictions. Progress depends on China following through on what it agreed.

brief.summary: Singapore's first data centre built under the stricter green rules has opened, targeting a power usage ratio of 1.2 against the required ceiling of 1.3. Grab was told to narrow its autonomous-vehicle trial in Punggol while LTA reviews a near-accident with a girl. A Commonwealth survey ranked Singapore first for youth AI readiness.

sections.title: Singapore AI startups
sections.subtitle: Funding, hiring, and what they're building

items.headline: Singapore chip startup Symatics unveils an AI processor architecture
items.summary: The company introduced what it calls an MPU, aimed at interactive AI and reasoning workloads. Tech in Asia's feed gives only a short description and I could not find a second report, so details are limited.

items.headline: Canlah AI builds agents to get firms noticed inside ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews
items.summary: The young Singapore startup helps companies stay visible as buyers shift from classic search to AI answers. It offers a free audit of how a brand appears and works in English and Chinese.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly raises another US$11 billion at a US$1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: The money is part of a round that has not closed and is expected to finish within weeks. The figure would put OpenAI well ahead of any other private AI company.

items.headline: Meta adds Spaces to its Muse assistant
items.summary: Spaces lets users have Muse build custom, app-like workspaces for whatever they need at the moment, such as a tracker or planner. It is another step in Meta turning Muse from a chatbot into an agent platform.

items.headline: OpenAI steps back from NDAs on data centre projects
items.summary: After voters this week pushed back on data centre expansion, OpenAI announced new commitments to host communities, including dropping the confidentiality agreements it used on local projects.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for US$500 million
items.summary: Clutch, backed by Lightspeed and SignalFire, was valued at only US$85 million in its last round, according to a source. The deal would be a big step up for the young company.

items.headline: Ramp data suggests AI spending has stalled just as Anthropic nears its IPO
items.summary: Usage keeps climbing but business spending has flattened, helped by price cuts and tighter cost controls at the biggest spenders. That could challenge investor assumptions about AI revenue.

items.headline: China reportedly recruited a Megaspeed executive to spy on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
items.summary: According to the New York Times, China's intelligence agency enlisted Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to monitor the Nvidia chief. It adds to tension over chips and trade between Washington and Beijing.

items.headline: Chinese video AI startup Sand AI raises US$200 million
items.summary: The round brings its funding over the past ten months to US$300 million, a sign of how heavily investors are backing Chinese video generation.

items.headline: DeepSeek's Harness tool reaches 1.54 million daily users, up 468 per cent
items.summary: The team says daily users were 271,000 on 30 September, so the product has added more than a million in just over a month.

items.headline: Nature Select, maker of AI social app Elys, raises over US$100 million
items.summary: The Qiming-backed Chinese developer closed a series A+ round. The size shows investor appetite for AI companion and social apps remains strong.

items.headline: Hua Hong wants a bigger role in silicon photonics for AI
items.summary: The chipmaker's chairman says it aims to make every silicon-based part inside optical modules, which move data between machines in AI data centres.
